record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: (“runs" conjecture, due to Kolpakov and Kucherov, [42]): For a binary alphabet, given word of length n the number of its runs is bounded by n.

evidence.quote: (“runs" conjecture, due to Kolpakov and Kucherov, [42]): For a binary alphabet, given word of length n the number of its runs is bounded by n.

artifact.status_search_result: The "runs" conjecture of Kolpakov and Kucherov was proved by Bannai, I, Inenaga, Nakashima, Takeda, and Tsuruta in "The 'Runs' Theorem" (arXiv:1406.0263, 2014; published versions follow). They established that the number of runs in any string of length $n$ is less than $n$, and subsequent refinements obtained sharper bounds (e.g. at most $(22/23)n$ for binary strings).

status_evidence.title: The "Runs" Theorem
status_evidence.snippet: We give a simple proof that the maximum number of runs in a string of length n is less than n, settling the so-called runs conjecture of Kolpakov and Kucherov (FOCS '99).
status_evidence.claim: The runs conjecture (number of runs < n) was proved.

status_evidence.title: The Runs Theorem and Beyond
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing the proof of the runs theorem, confirming the upper bound of n on the number of runs.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the conjecture is now a theorem.
